_comment: BAND-SPLIT. Band-local clusters for band2_stone_and_root. `order` is this entry's index in the merged array and is the ONLY thing that decides merge position -- never file order, never band order. Existing entries keep the index they had before the split because the merged array order is the order props are added to the scene tree, and Godot silently auto-renames same-named siblings by that order. A new entry in this band takes an unused order in this band's reserved range 2000-2999, which no other band can collide with; do not renumber an existing one.

clusters.name: quarry_station
clusters._why: SD16, and the cluster EV7-remainder listed as still unbuilt and left to this item. The Old Quarry's own working face, abandoned mid-shift: the gear a crew leaves when the work stops rather than when it finishes. It sits on the quarry floor between the two foundations and the conduit head, so the walk in reads working face -> old foundations -> Team Tether hardware, which is the order §32's reveal ladder wants that rung told in. Every model is one the settlement already uses (D24, one prop family); nothing here is new.

props.name: OldQuarryWorkWagon
props._why: OLD-QUARRY-WORK-CART-R32-0913. The installed wagon sits five metres east of the haul-apron endpoint on the southeast work shoulder beside the single shift lantern. That keeps a readable visual handoff while its production collision no longer covers the apron from every honest south-road view. The retained scale and 58-degree wheel/body presentation preserve the extraction read without competing with the worked face or conduit head.
the cluster's anchor -- a crate of cut stone still standing where it was filled
set against the first crate's side, not merely near it -- EV7-clusters-fix's own finding: a loose arc of props reads as dumped, a touching pile reads as one load
water for the crew, kept with the load
leaning where it was set down, pitched off vertical against the rock -- the one prop in the cluster that names the work, and the reason the player's own pickaxe is the tool the rootstone wants
tipped over a couple of paces off the pile, so the group has an edge instead of a boundary
somebody's pack, still here -- the detail that makes the site abandoned rather than merely disused

SITE-DRESSING: cut-face spoil, largest of the set, between the working pile and the conduit head (404,1804) -- what a quarry actually leaves is broken rock, not four identical boulders on a lawn. Same textured Rock_Medium family band1's fire ring already proved through props.gd (environment/nature's own untextured rock pack is the one that fails, per that band's own record).

SITE-DRESSING: second spoil piece, deliberately a different model AND a different scale/rotation band from its neighbour -- the two-identical-rocks-at-near-identical-rotation defect this pass exists to fix.
SITE-DRESSING: spoil at the foot of the north-west foundation (397,1805) -- rubble a crew clearing that ruin's own footing would have piled here, not carried off.
SITE-DRESSING: smaller chip toward the second foundation (404,1794), the one piece in this set scaled as debris rather than a boulder -- extraction leaves a size gradient, not one repeated stone.

SITE-DRESSING: closes the working face's own cut-face read -- set behind the crate pile from the approach so the crew reads as having worked INTO the rock, not merely stacked crates on grass beside it.

clusters.name: old_quarry_cut_face
clusters._why: OLD-QUARRY-TERRACE-R19-0912. R18's independent production review retained the connected face but rejected its low, uniformly rounded berm silhouette. Five more deeply buried, vertically exposed rear masses now form a tall irregular cut. Four broad mid shelves overlap their feet, and three lower toe ledges step toward the haul floor, producing three readable value bands and repeated horizontal working levels rather than a row of stones. This remains the installed Meadows rock family; all masses stay outside the Band 2 spine and preserve the wagon, foundations, resources and conduit corridors.

props.name: OldQuarryCutFaceWest
props._why: Tall buried western shoulder begins the exposed cut; the brighter warm-grey crown separates from the forest at night.

props.name: OldQuarryCutFaceMidWest
props._why: Second tall exposure removes the old grass notch and raises an uneven worked crown above the lower shelves.

props.name: OldQuarryCutFaceCentre
props._why: Highest central exposure is buried past its rounded foot and supplies the face's dominant vertical cut.

props.name: OldQuarryCutFaceMidEast
props._why: Fourth tall exposure turns the cut toward the active floor without falling back into a countable boulder row.

props.name: OldQuarryCutFaceEast
props._why: Eastern shoulder retains enough height to close the wall before handing down to the worked shelves.

props.name: OldQuarryCutBenchWest
props._why: Broad western shelf masks the rear wall foot and begins the darker middle working level.

props.name: OldQuarryCutBenchCentre
props._why: Second broad shelf overlaps the western ledge and carries a continuous horizontal break through the face.

props.name: OldQuarryCutBenchEast
props._why: Third broad shelf keeps the darker exposed seam unbroken across the turn toward the work floor.

props.name: OldQuarryCutBenchToe
props._why: Eastern middle shelf completes the second visible level and overlaps the first low toe.

props.name: OldQuarryLowerLedgeWest
props._why: Low western toe creates a second repeated horizontal break below the dark middle seam.

props.name: OldQuarryLowerLedgeCentre
props._why: Centre-west toe overlaps its neighbour so the lowest working level reads as a shelf, not spoil.

props.name: OldQuarryLowerLedgeMidEast
props._why: A fourth toe is necessary to keep the lower shelf physically continuous while turning toward the route-safe wagon handoff.

props.name: OldQuarryLowerLedgeEast
props._why: Brightest low toe uses the previously proven route-safe seat to finish within one visual step of the wagon.

clusters.name: ranger_camp
clusters._why: MQ2B, docs/specs/MEADOWS_MACRO_LAYOUT.md section 5 camp table: 'a ring of stones, a collapsed lean-to, and someone's kit. Salvage, not shelter' -- the ranger_camp_spur loop's own destination (terrain_playground.json trail.loops, leaves the spine at [-150,2210], rejoins at [-310,2320]), authored bare until now. Placed a few metres off the loop's own painted road, at its midpoint, so the road passes beside the camp rather than through it -- something you notice on the spur, not something you walk over. NOTE ON SUBSTITUTION: the shipped prop family (assets/props/quaternius_fantasy, the only pack props.gd's loader reads) has no stone or tent/frame mesh, so the fire ring and lean-to described above are read through what the family actually has -- a toppled cot standing in for the collapsed shelter, an open cabinet for the ring of stones' absence, same reasoning old_quarry.gd's own cluster already leans on for 'somebody's pack, still here'. D24's one-prop-family rule holds: nothing here is new. ROUND 3 (OPS15 blind-critic loop): round 2's critic called this 'three props dropped at a way-point, not a camp anyone lives in' and named the missing thing specifically -- seating. Added a bench and a log, both already in the same pack, so the cluster reads as a place someone actually sat rather than a supply drop.

rest._why:
T5-CADENCE. T4-REGIONS scored band 2's camp/recovery row FAIL for the same reason it failed band 1's and band 3's: nine props including a bed, an anvil and a whetstone, a named map landmark (`band2_ranger_camp`), and no interaction path in `props.gd` at all.

WHAT THIS OVERTURNS, named rather than quietly overwritten. This cluster's own `_why` above reads 'Salvage, not shelter', and the site was deliberately authored as an ABANDONED camp. The re-read that follows the audit is that the two are not in tension: a ranger's camp with a cot, a bench, a whetstone and an anvil is exactly the kind of place a traveller puts back into use for a night, and it sits on the `ranger_camp_spur` loop -- content the player goes out of their way for. What it stops being is a camp that punishes the detour with a refusal. The collapse is still read by the toppled cabinet, the emptied crate, the dropped bag and the tipped bucket; the cot is what a user of the site would have righted first, and now has.

SITED at the new fire, on the cluster's open side away from the cot and the toppled cabinet.
rest.label: Rest until morning

creature_bed._why: The cot, righted and made real. Replaces the toppled `Bed_Twin1` that stood at this exact spot -- the same position, the same yaw, upright instead of rolled onto its side -- and the mesh changes with it, from the furniture pack's human twin bed to `generated_camp/camp_bed.glb`. That swap is not incidental: `creature_bed.gd`'s own header records two independent blind critics reading `Bed_Twin1` as 'a human bed labelled creature bed', and this camp's own `_why` records the twin bed as a SUBSTITUTION made because the shipped prop family had no lean-to; the camp set has since shipped a lashed-log bed that belongs to this game. One fewer stand-in, not one more asset.

props._why: T5-CADENCE. The 'ring of stones' this cluster's own `_why` names as the first of its three authored elements and then records as UNBUILDABLE: 'the shipped prop family has no stone or tent/frame mesh, so the fire ring and lean-to described above are read through what the family actually has -- ... an open cabinet for the ring of stones' absence.' That is no longer true. `campfire_stone_ring.glb` has since shipped from the owner-referenced camp set (docs/specs/ASSET_LEDGER.md) and band 1's trail camp and band 4's ridge camp both use it. Nothing new is generated or sourced; the substitution note above is simply spent. Scaled between band 1's rest camp (1.05) and band 4's patrol posting (0.55): a ranger's own small fire. Sited on the open side, 4m clear of the cot and past the crate/bag pile, on ground nothing else stands on.

T5-CADENCE. The fire inside that ring, the same solved combination band 1 and band 4 both use (`Bonfire_Fire.obj`'s real `Fire` surface + `ignite()` + `campfire_glow.gd`'s light/embers/smoke overlay). A rest point with no fire is the thing a player walks past: the fire is this world's universal 'you can stop here' cue, it is what makes the camp findable off the spur at dusk, and the audit's whole complaint about these sites is that they advertise rest without offering it. Scale matches the ring.
toppled beside the cot, door-side down -- whatever it held is long gone or scattered
supply crate, emptied out -- nobody restocked it before leaving
someone's kit, still here -- the same detail that makes the quarry site read abandoned rather than merely disused, told again in a different place
tipped a couple of paces from the cot, dry long before the camp was left
a ranger's own tool, set down and never picked back up
what lashed the lean-to together, come loose with it
ROUND 3. Faces the cot, close enough to have shared the same small fire the missing ring of stones would have held -- the seating the critic's round-2 pass named as absent
ROUND 3. A second, lower seat opposite the bench -- two ways to sit reads as a place people actually gathered, not one bench posed alone

props.name: RangerCampCollapsedShelter
props._why: RANGER-CAMP-ARRIVAL-R2-0911. The established camp is ten knee-high props plus fire; in production arrival frames it reads as a bench pile until the label. The installed patched-canvas camp_tent supplies the missing silhouette without inventing a new prop family, pitched nearly flat with a slight roll so it reads as a collapsed lashed shelter rather than an intact place to sleep. Its imported local bounds are y [-0.6114,0.5973], z [-0.9486,0.9481]; after the authored 68-degree pitch and 8-degree roll, the old scale/sink buried about 0.86m of the collapsed canvas below terrain. Scale 1.08 and sink -1.22 leave the transformed lower edge about 0.02m into the ground, revealing the existing lifted corner without floating it. The centre stays at the proven open-side position: the conservative 1.35m footprint edge remains 7.25m from the rest centre, 6.80m from crafting, and 8.95m from the ranger spur.

clusters.name: quarry_supply_cache
clusters._why: BAND2-63. `terrain_playground.json`'s `ranger_camp_spur` loop names its own reason for existing as 'the abandoned camp, AND THE FIRST EVIDENCE TEAM TETHER HAS BEEN MOVING MATERIAL' -- the camp above delivers the first half; nothing in the band ever delivered the second. Same crate the Old Quarry's own `quarry_station` cluster uses for cut stone (`Crate_Wooden`, see that cluster's own note), so a player who has already read that pile at the quarry reads THIS one the same way without being told twice -- material moving from the working face, through here, toward wherever Team Tether takes it. Sited on the spur's own path (-210,2230), well short of the ranger camp itself (-259,2256) so this reads as something found ALONG the way rather than part of the camp -- somebody hauling a load stopped here, or was stopped here, and never came back for it.

props._why: the anchor -- a second crate of cut stone, the same load the quarry's own crate carries, this one part-way down the spur instead of on the quarry floor

ROUND 2 (blind self-pass): round 1's 70-degree pitch did not read as toppled against a crate model that is already boxy from most angles -- pushed to a full 90 so the crate's OWN long edge breaks the ground plane the standing one sits flat on, the same silhouette cue a fallen box gives at a glance. Sink raised to match, so the corner that is now the lowest point does not float.
what lashed the load down for hauling, come loose with it -- the detail that says CARRIED rather than simply left, matching the loop's own words

clusters.name: warrens_vault_signal
clusters._why: F03#0 lure (coordinator grant, 2026-09-26: one marker above the Warrens vault entrance, visible from 50 m or more, existing prop family, no red). The round-5 code-blind judge could not find the Warrens from the road: 'the site only appears once the player is already beside it'. A waylight post at the mouth, the Rise trail's own Torch_Metal waylight at post height, carrying the same signal-smoke column Bram's and Doss's fires use (campfire_glow.configure_smoke via props.gd), so the dig reads from the road by day (smoke) and by night (flame). Placed at the warren's local (+5.5, -3): in front of the mouth, beside the 8 m apron on the road side, rotated by the site's own 315 degree yaw about burrow_warrens.json site.at (-357, 2610). No staging logic touched.

props.name: WarrensVaultSignalPost
props._why: Waylight post and signal column; see the cluster note.
